a.xlink:title: The affinity term is unconditional in the pack's `modify_pod_hook`, so RWX homes would still be pinned pointlessly. Removing the pin is a Data Science Pack change — a config switch, or keying off the home volume's access mode — and must be raised with the pack's owners early, since without it the RWX-homes shape keeps the constraint it exists to remove.

a.xlink:title: RWX homes remove a cluster of separate problems rather than mitigating each one.

a.xlink:title: The pack establishes POSIX ownership on the home volume through kubelet-applied `fsGroup: 100` with `fsGroupChangePolicy: OnRootMismatch`, paired with a hardcoded `umask 0002` and setgid 2775 directories — the umask deliberately not a tunable knob, because it is coupled to the shared-storage setgid design. That is a block-volume mechanism: NFS-backed CSI drivers report no fsGroup support, so the kubelet does not apply it and ownership has to be established by the filesystem instead — FSx for OpenZFS uid/gid mapping and root-squash settings, or EFS access points enforcing a POSIX user. The RWX-homes shape therefore has to rebuild the ownership model on a different mechanism rather than carry it over, and re-verify the setgid propagation `/shared` already depends on against the appliance's export semantics. A second pack-side prerequisite alongside Affinity pin needs an upstream switch, and the reason the POSIX behavior gate names fsGroup explicitly.
